title: The 10 Best Drywall Screw Guns
subtitle: Cordless and corded drywall screw guns for hanging sheetrock, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A drywall screw gun sets every screw at the same depth so you don't tear the paper or leave screws proud. We ranked 10 best-sellers from DEWALT, Milwaukee, RYOBI and a budget brand on rating, review volume and features (a brushless motor, cordless power, push or auto start and a battery in the box).

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX XR Brushless Drywall Screwgun, Tool Only (DCF630B)

specs.extras: 4 modes incl. PushStart and lock-on, adjustable nosecone, belt clip

products.verdict: The best-selling and most-reviewed drywall screw gun here: brushless, 2.6 lb, with four modes including PushStart, where the motor only spins when the screw meets the board.
products.best_for: DEWALT owners hanging drywall, from one room to a whole house.

products.name: DEWALT Drywall Screw Gun, 6.0-Amp (DW255)
products.verdict: DEWALT's classic corded drywall gun: 5,300 RPM for fast production hanging and a set-and-forget nosepiece for consistent screw depth.
products.best_for: Drywall hangers who want a cheap, proven corded gun.
products.skip_if: You hate dragging a cord across the room.
pros: Lowest price of the brand-name guns

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FUEL Drywall Screw Gun, Tool Only (2866-20)

specs.extras: Auto Start mode, LED on the foot, up to 64 sheets per XC5.0 charge

products.verdict: Milwaukee's M18 FUEL screw gun with an Auto Start mode that keeps the motor off until the screw touches the board, which Milwaukee says triples runtime.

products.name: RYOBI ONE+ 18V Cordless Brushless Drywall Screw Gun, Tool Only (P225)

products.name: DEWALT Drywall Screw Gun, Variable Speed Reversible, 6.5-Amp (DW276)
products.verdict: A slower, higher-torque corded screw gun for decks and heavy-gauge steel studs as well as drywall, with a metal gear housing.
products.best_for: Framers driving into steel studs and decking.

products.name: Hoteche 4.5-Amp Drywall Screw Gun, Variable Speed 0-4500 RPM, 1/4" Chuck
products.verdict: The cheapest screw gun here, a corded 4.5-amp gun for about $40 with spare brushes in the box.

products.skip_if: You hang drywall often; it's rated 3.8 stars.

avoid.name: MAXXT 20V Brushless Drywall Screw Gun (Tool Only), 2-in-1 Screwdriver and Router
avoid.verdict: A 2-in-1 screw gun and router whose listing contradicts itself on what's in the box, with the lowest rating of the guns we looked at.
reasons: The title says 'Tool Only', but the spec table lists 'Batteries' as the included component.
The model number is two part numbers joined with a plus sign, and the spec table gives the 'maximum chuck size' as 5.7 centimeters, which is the longest screw it sets, not a chuck size.
It's rated 2.8 stars. The RYOBI P225 is brushless, cheaper, and rated 4.4.

buyers_guide.q: Why not just use a drill?
buyers_guide.a: A drywall screw gun has a depth-setting nosecone that sinks each screw just below the paper without tearing it, and a clutch that disengages when the screw is set. It's faster and gives a cleaner finish than a drill.
Corded guns are cheap and run all day. Cordless guns are lighter and free you from the cord on ladders and ceilings, and modern brushless ones get through dozens of sheets per charge.

buyers_guide.q: What are PushStart and Auto Start?
buyers_guide.a: The trigger stays locked on, but the motor only spins when you press a screw into the board. It's quieter and saves battery.
Around 4,000 to 5,300 RPM suits drywall. Slower, 2,500 RPM guns like the DW276 and DW257 have more torque for decking and heavy-gauge steel.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a collated attachment?
buyers_guide.a: For whole houses, a collated (strip-fed) attachment speeds up hanging a lot. For a room or two, loose screws are fine.
